tasks.short: Answer buyer questions about products, prices, availability, uses and credit terms.

steps.what: Clarify the buyer's question and intended use.
Check account prices, stock and approved credit terms in the {ERP}.
Find product uses, limitations and warranty guidance in approved documents.

loop.input: Clarified question and retrieved passages from current approved documents.
loop.output: Relevant guidance with document version, passage citations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify citations and document versions; reject unsupported statements and conflicting guidance.
loop.stop: At most two retrieval rounds and one extraction; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Product uses and limitations are often buried in prose. Structured facts use direct lookup.

steps.what: Explain the answer and resolve questions about the buyer's situation.
Send written confirmation of the answer and supporting information.
Record the question, answer and follow-up in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: An answer desk in the {CRM} retrieves account-specific commercial facts from the {ERP} and cited guidance from {DOCS}. Configured templates assemble confirmations for representative approval in {EMAIL}, then update the {CRM}; a bounded extraction loop handles prose manuals. A small {BI} view groups recorded questions to reveal recurring information gaps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account prices and stock sat apart from product documents. Keeping access permissions, document versions and answers aligned required integration and upkeep.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and templates handle factual lookup. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded extraction helps with prose manuals.
tasks.still_hard: Fresh availability, account-specific terms, conflicting manuals and unusual product uses still need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a simple question hides a suitability concern, commercial objection or damaged relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on which recurring product-information gaps to fix.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time searching and more time resolving uncertain uses and commercial exceptions. They can prioritise information improvements; pricing and credit authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check availability and explain order status.
reach.learn: Distinguish physical stock, available-to-promise stock and unconfirmed delivery estimates.

evidence.claim: Record-based answers can use deterministic lookup; prose manuals may need bounded extraction.
Elfsquad connects product configuration with commercial systems, supporting adjacent product-information lookup.
The documented chatbot fare dispute illustrates exposure from incorrect customer-facing answers.
Customer-facing AI interaction requires disclosure under EU AI Act Article 50.

assumptions: This is a typical mixed channel workflow; time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The bounded model output remains internal. Written confirmations use approved templates and a human release gate.
Structured question fields replace duplicate logging without assuming call recording.
GDPR applies to buyer and employee records. EU AI Act duties depend on deployment; national rules determine consultation requirements.
Effort ranges assume usable interfaces and include access, permissions, rollout and consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which account prices, credit terms and stock fields are authoritative and accessible?
Which manuals have owners, versions and approved translations?
Can the existing {CRM} configure templates, interaction capture and account-level permissions?
Would the proposed reporting introduce employee monitoring requiring national consultation?
research_questions: How often do questions require interpretation beyond approved documents?
What data freshness is needed before an availability answer becomes misleading?
Which question categories can use fixed templates without a model?
new_work: Resolve conflicting documents and missing account facts.
Maintain document ownership, lookup mappings and templates.
Sample cited guidance and review recurring unanswered questions.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable products based on the buyer's needs, constraints and preferences.

steps.what: Discuss intended use, budget, delivery needs and preferences with the buyer.
Review the buyer's previous purchases and recorded preferences in the {CRM}.
Compare catalogue specifications and identify products meeting the stated constraints.
Choose a recommendation and identify trade-offs or unanswered suitability questions.
Explain the recommendation, demonstrate relevant features and discuss alternatives.
Record the recommendation, buyer feedback and next action in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A structured needs form in the {CRM} feeds a deterministic comparison tool using approved catalogue attributes from {DOCS} and current price and availability from the {ERP}. It filters hard constraints, shows trade-offs and reruns when requirements change; the representative chooses and explains the recommendation. Selected products and structured feedback populate a reviewable {CRM} record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Catalogue attributes were inconsistent, and buyer preferences lived in conversations. Building and maintaining a useful comparison tool required substantial manual mapping.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small comparison tool cheaper to build. Explicit product constraints and structured needs capture provide the underlying logic.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete specifications, unstated preferences, unfamiliar uses and competing priorities resist simple scoring.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what the buyer values, challenge an unsuitable request and explain a trade-off credibly.

ambition.what: Reassess product fit during the discussion whenever budget or delivery requirements change.

tasks.altitude: The representative compares alternatives during the buyer discussion instead of researching them afterwards. They retain recommendation responsibility; no new commercial approval rights are assumed.

reach.task: Validate compatibility and unusual product applications.
reach.learn: Separate hard exclusions from preferences and recognise when specialist validation is necessary.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad supports rule-based product configuration connected to commercial systems.
Explicit constraints can narrow a shortlist without automating the buyer's preferences or the representative's judgement.
The proposed time reductions and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: Most recommendations concern established catalogue goods with identifiable constraints.
Automated filtering covers explicit requirements only; missing critical attributes trigger specialist review.
Existing configuration features are checked before building a comparison tool.
Structured notes are captured during the discussion; automatic recording or transcription is not assumed.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine consultation where employee data use changes.
Effort includes initial catalogue mapping, access, user trials and applicable consultation.
unknowns: Are product specifications available as maintained structured attributes?
Does existing software already provide adequate configuration or comparison?
Are purchase history and account preferences accessible in the {CRM}?
research_questions: Which constraints eliminate unsuitable products reliably?
How often do experienced representatives reject a technically valid shortlist?
Which missing attributes cause the most manual research?
new_work: Maintain catalogue attributes and hard exclusions.
Investigate empty or unexpectedly broad shortlists.
Check whether changing specifications invalidate existing comparison rules.

tasks.short: Prepare and explain quotes covering prices, terms, warranties and estimated delivery dates.

steps.what: Clarify quantities, product choices, delivery requirements and requested terms with the buyer.
Check account pricing, stock, lead times and existing credit terms in the {ERP}.
Calculate line prices, discounts, freight and quote totals in a spreadsheet.
Select approved warranty and contract wording for the proposed sale.
Review and approve requested discounts outside the representative's authority.
Decide whether to approve requested credit terms outside existing account limits.
Assemble the quote document with approved prices, terms and delivery estimates.
Explain the proposed offer and negotiate requested changes with the buyer.
Check the final quote and send it to the buyer.

tasks.design: Configure quoting in the {CRM} or {ERP} with approved product rules, calculations and templates from {DOCS}; use a deterministic connector where existing links are insufficient. The {WORKFLOW} routes discount and credit exceptions to their authorised approvers, invalidates approvals after material changes and requires representative approval before {EMAIL} release. Price-version changes in the {ERP} flag affected open quotes in the {CRM} for repricing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices, terms and approvals were maintained separately. Bespoke quoting logic and reliable links were costly to implement and keep aligned.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration handles much of the quoting logic. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connectors, validation and document assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Negotiated exceptions, uncertain supply dates, inconsistent price data and non-standard contract language remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the commercial trade-off, negotiate credibly and avoid promises the business cannot fulfil.

ambition.what: Reprice affected open quotes when supplier price changes reach the {ERP}.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time calculating and assembling documents, and more time negotiating viable offers. Existing discount and credit limits remain in force; no new approval rights are assumed.

reach.task: Review discount exceptions and commercial exposure.
reach.learn: Explain margin, freight and payment-term effects when proposing a concession.

reach.task: Convert an accepted quote into an accurate order.
reach.learn: Maintain item identifiers, quote versions and approval references through the handoff.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad provides rule-based configuration and quoting linked to commercial systems.
The ZARGES vendor case reports quoting time falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds.
Structured quoting calculations, clause selection and approval routing generally do not need a model.

assumptions: The typical baseline uses the {ERP} for facts, with a spreadsheet bridging calculations and document preparation.
Approval steps are conditional; their time shares represent effort across the quote portfolio.
Negotiated changes repeat affected calculation and approval steps before release.
Only approved clause variants are selected automatically; non-standard terms require separate authorised review.
Unconfirmed delivery dates remain estimates. Existing account credit terms are retrieved without introducing automated credit scoring.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements apply. National rules govern consultation where relevant.
Effort assumes configurable quoting is available and includes access, approval testing and rollout.
unknowns: What quoting configuration and integration features are already licensed?
Which discounts and terms can the representative approve?
Can the {ERP} distinguish confirmed delivery promises from estimates?
Are supplier price changes versioned against open quotes?
research_questions: Which quote variants account for most manual assembly?
How often do changes invalidate earlier approvals?
Which calculation discrepancies most often cause order-entry rework?
new_work: Maintain pricing rules, templates and approval thresholds.
Resolve missing prices and uncertain delivery dates.
Review exceptions and final quote release.
Review repricing alerts and decide whether to revise open offers.
Check that negotiated changes invalidate affected approvals.

tasks.short: Support buyers after a sale, resolve problems and coordinate agreed remedies.

steps.what: Listen to the buyer's problem and clarify its impact and desired outcome.
Review the account history and link the issue to the relevant order.
Check product guidance, warranty coverage and relevant support procedures.

loop.input: Case brief and current approved product, warranty and support documents.
loop.output: Cited procedures, possible exclusions and questions needing human assessment.
loop.check: Verify product and document versions, exact source passages and applicability dates; do not infer entitlement.
loop.stop: At most two retrieval rounds and one extraction; unresolved coverage or conflicting procedures go to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative fault descriptions and procedural documents require language matching; fixed identifiers use direct lookup.

steps.what: Send the issue and evidence to operations for investigation.
Investigate the issue and confirm feasible remedies and timing.
Discuss the options and agree a remedy or support plan with the buyer.
Record agreed actions, owners and due dates in the {CRM}.
Send the agreed follow-up and check whether the issue is resolved.

tasks.design: A linked case view in the {CRM} reads orders from the {ERP}, operational status from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and cited support guidance from {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes internal requests, tracks owners and deadlines, and prepares approved-template follow-ups for representative release through {EMAIL}. Confirmed delivery events also create first-use check-in tasks in the {CRM}, while investigation and remedy conversations remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case context was scattered across messages, account records and operational records. Follow-up depended on individual memory and manual chasing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured cases, event triggers and templates already cover much of the coordination. Cheaper integrations and bounded document extraction reduce preparation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Physical faults, disputed responsibility, supplier dependencies and rebuilding trust still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the buyer's frustration, take credible responsibility and negotiate a remedy that both sides can accept.

ambition.what: Scheduled first-use support for first-time business buyers.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time reconstructing cases and chasing updates, with more time for difficult recovery conversations and planned support. Remedy and compensation authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Plan post-sale check-ins and confirm that the buyer receives the intended benefit.
reach.learn: Use milestones and buyer outcomes to structure useful follow-up conversations.

reach.task: Assess escalated complaints and proposed commercial remedies.
reach.learn: Present customer impact, feasible options and commercial consequences clearly.

evidence.claim: Case linking, internal routing, deadlines and template follow-ups can use deterministic workflows.
Bounded extraction can prepare cited guidance while leaving entitlement and remedy decisions to people.
The digest contains no documented case measuring this complete post-sale support workflow.

assumptions: The baseline uses the {CRM} and internal messages for coordination; an existing {HELPDESK} should be configured instead if it already owns support cases.
The operations step covers investigation and feasible options, not every downstream repair, replacement or refund activity.
Structured remedy fields are confirmed by the representative; no automatic call recording is assumed.
Human conversations act within existing authority. Out-of-authority compensation requires the existing approval process before commitment.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements apply. National rules determine employee consultation and monitoring restrictions.
Effort includes case permissions, access, consultation where applicable, realistic exception trials and rollout.
unknowns: Does the {CRM} or {HELPDESK} own the authoritative support case?
Can customer accounts, orders and operational incidents be linked reliably?
Who may authorise replacements, refunds and compensation?
Are delivery events and remedy completion updates reliable enough to trigger follow-up?
What access and national consultation requirements apply to shared case reporting?
research_questions: Which delays arise from missing context rather than physical investigation?
Which support procedures can be retrieved reliably by product and issue type?
When do first-time buyers benefit most from a first-use check-in?
new_work: Review case updates and customer follow-ups.
Resolve unmatched orders and contradictory support guidance.
Maintain routing, escalation paths and document versions.
Check overdue actions and delivery-trigger failures.
Conduct the new first-use check-ins and record their outcomes.

role.altitude: The week shifts from searching, calculating and chasing to buyer discovery, commercial negotiation and relationship recovery. Recommendation responsibility and existing approval limits remain; no additional pricing, credit or compensation rights are assumed.
reach: Order clerk: improve the handoff from recommendation and quote to an accurate order.
Sales engineer: recognise compatibility constraints and escalate unusual uses with better evidence.
Sales manager: present clearer discount and remedy decisions with their commercial consequences.
Sales representative of services: structure useful post-sale check-ins around buyer outcomes.
skills_to_grow: Turn buyer needs into explicit constraints without losing context.
Read pricing, availability and delivery data critically.
Prepare concise exception requests for authorised approvers.
Evaluate cited guidance and recognise unsupported conclusions.
Use recurring questions and support cases to improve buyer information.
role.ambitious_version: Offer smaller business buyers the same preparation and continuity as larger accounts: informed product comparisons, reliable quotes and scheduled first-use support. Expand through reusable rules, shared records and targeted human attention.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
